site.name: pelagic
site.summary: pelagic-clone Marketing site (landing page) for the fictional open-source vector database Pelagic. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Single-page landing: top nav + animated GitHub-stars counter pill; hero with title, dual CTAs, `pip install` copy strip, rotating benchmark numbers, right-side 4-language (Python / Node / Go / curl) code tabs; Trusted-by logo row; 3 core-feature cards; Ingest → Index → Query three-step flow; architecture SVG diagram; customer quote cards; left Blog 5 posts + right Changelog 5 entries dual feed; 4-column footer with sitemap | | `styles.css` | Brand color #0E5C8A deep-sea blue; Inter + JetBrains Mono; responsive at 3 breakpoints (>1100 / 880–1100 / <880) | | `script.js` | Stars-counter 1.2s eased animation; code tabs switch Python / Node / Go / curl; benchmark rows rotate every 2.5s; `pip install pelagic` copy toast; fictional-logo rendering |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full pelagic system, prioritizing the primary landing flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Pelagic landing page presents a visually appealing and responsive single-page design, but suffers from significant navigational and functional gaps. While interactive components like the code snippet switcher and toast notifications work well, numerous critical links—including primary CTAs to GitHub and internal anchor links—are broken or missing targets. Furthermore, the mobile experience is hindered by undersized touch targets and legibility issues with complex diagrams.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively validate the single-page landing experience of Pelagic, focusing on interactive components, dynamic animations, and responsive layout scaling.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will begin on desktop by interacting with custom JS components, notably the code snippet tabs and the copy-to-clipboard function. It will then verify internal navigation anchors and the rendering of complex content blocks like the architecture diagram and dual feeds. Finally, the run will switch to a mobile viewport to investigate flagged tap-target warnings and ensure the layout gracefully degrades.
assumptions: The site consists entirely of a single index.html page, so navigation links (Product, Docs, Pricing) likely rely on anchor scrolling or are placeholder links.
The 'copy install command' functionality should provide some visual feedback (like a toast) when clicked.
The code tabs (python, node, go, curl) toggle visibility of different text blocks within the same container without page reloads.
risk_hotspots: Small tap targets on top navigation and code tabs, especially problematic on mobile.
Horizontal overflow or clipping of the code block on narrow viewports.
Stacking behavior of multi-column sections (features, customer quotes, footer) on mobile.
JS errors that might break the tab switching or copy functionality.

phases.title: Desktop Interactive Components
phases.objective: Validate JS-driven interactive elements like code tabs and the copy button.
key_checks: Click through 'node', 'go', and 'curl' tabs to ensure the code snippet text updates accordingly.
Click the 'Copy install command' button and observe UI for a success toast or state change.
exit_criteria: All four code tabs successfully display different content.
Copy button interaction is completed and recorded.

phases.title: Desktop Navigation & Layout Flow
phases.objective: Ensure header links work and content sections render correctly as the user scrolls.
key_checks: Click navigation links (Product, Docs, Pricing, Blog) to confirm anchor scrolling behavior.
Verify visibility of the Trusted-by logo row, architecture SVG, and dual Blog/Changelog feeds.
exit_criteria: Page scrolled to bottom, verifying all major content sections are visible and structured well.

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness & Tap Targets
phases.objective: Evaluate mobile layout degradation and specifically test elements flagged for small tap targets.
key_checks: Verify if top navigation collapses into a hamburger menu or remains as small links.
Check if the hero section text and code block stack vertically without horizontal scrolling.
Attempt to tap the code language tabs (python, node, etc.) on mobile to assess usability.
Verify multi-column sections (features, footer) collapse to single columns.
exit_criteria: Mobile layout captured from top to bottom, with interaction attempts on the previously flagged small tap targets.

coverage_targets.features: Exercise code tabs, copy functionality, and anchor navigation.
coverage_targets.mobile: Validate layout breakpoints and re-test interactive tabs for usability.

notes: Pay attention to the rotating benchmark numbers and star counter animation during initial load; capture early screenshots if possible.

findings.user_goal: Access the project's source code and community to evaluate the open-source tool.
findings.problem: Critical call-to-action buttons and external links, such as 'View on GitHub', the 'GitHub stars' badge, and various community footer links, act as dead links (href="#").
findings.evidence: In step 49, clicking 'View on GitHub' merely appended '#' to the URL. The same behavior was observed for the 'GitHub stars' header button (step 13) and footer links like 'Discord' and 'Forum'.
findings.why_it_matters: For an open-source database, examining the GitHub repository and community is a primary user objective. Dead links completely block this evaluation path and severely damage trust in the product.
findings.suggestion: Update the href attributes for all GitHub, community, and external links to point to their actual destinations, or remove/disable them if the resources do not exist yet.

findings.user_goal: Navigate to specific sections of the landing page, such as getting started instructions or pricing details.
findings.problem: Several main navigation links update the URL hash but fail to scroll the page because their target sections do not exist.
findings.evidence: Clicking the 'Quickstart' header link updates the URL to '#quickstart' (step 48), and clicking 'Pricing' updates it to '#pricing' (step 7-12 chunk), but neither action results in the page scrolling to relevant content.
findings.why_it_matters: Broken internal anchors create a confusing user experience. Users click expecting immediate access to vital information but are left stranded, making the site feel unfinished.
findings.suggestion: Ensure that all internal anchor links point to valid HTML elements with corresponding 'id' attributes on the page. If the content for 'Quickstart' or 'Pricing' is not yet built, remove the links from the navigation.

findings.user_goal: Easily tap interactive elements on a mobile touchscreen.
findings.problem: Multiple interactive elements, including code language tabs, the 'Copy' button, and footer links, have tap target sizes significantly below the recommended 44px minimum for touch interfaces.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings highlight that the code tabs (e.g., 'python', 'node') are only 32px tall, the 'Copy' button is 25px tall, and footer links are 29px tall. This was actively tested on the mobile viewport in steps 31-36 and 43-48.
findings.why_it_matters: Undersized touch targets lead to 'fat-finger' errors, where users accidentally click the wrong language tab or link, causing frustration and a feeling of poor mobile optimization.
findings.suggestion: Increase the vertical padding or minimum height of these interactive elements so they meet or exceed the 44px touch target guideline on mobile breakpoints.

findings.user_goal: Understand the system architecture by viewing the provided diagram on a mobile device.
findings.problem: The Architecture SVG diagram scales down proportionally to fit the narrow mobile screen width, causing the internal text labels to become extremely small.
findings.evidence: During mobile viewport exploration (steps 37-42), it was noted that while the Architecture SVG avoids horizontal overflow by scaling down, the internal text of the diagram blocks becomes 'very small and potentially illegible.'
findings.why_it_matters: The architecture diagram is a key selling point for a technical database product. If users cannot read it on mobile, they miss critical technical information and context.
findings.suggestion: Provide a mobile-specific layout for the architecture diagram (e.g., stacking the components vertically) or place the SVG in a horizontally scrollable container with a visual cue, allowing it to maintain a readable size.
